Baram v0.8.0 lets scripts and AI clients read your notes: the program that opens the editor
now also answers from a terminal, and serves the same read-only commands to AI clients that
speak MCP, such as Claude Code. Plugins can put their commands in the right-click and slash
menus, draw code blocks, show a sidebar panel, mark files in the file tree and read your links,
tags and tasks, and you can give their commands keyboard shortcuts. A new **Mode** setting keeps
a theme that has both a light and a dark palette in the one you choose. Most of the rest are
fixes for ways Baram could lose or rewrite your text: when updating, in file windows and
Untitled tabs, when creating a file, and when saving.

If you are updating from v0.7.7, these are the changes most likely to catch you out:

- **Save your open documents before you press Install & Restart.** v0.7.7 runs this update
  itself, and it installs and restarts without asking about unsaved changes (see **Updating**
  at the end).
- The **System (Auto)** theme card is now called **Baram Default**, and a new **Mode** row sits
  below the gallery.
- **Renaming a file no longer moves it to another folder**: a new name containing `/` is
  refused.
- A front-matter tag written with `#`, as in `tags: ["#solo"]`, is now the same tag as `#solo`
  in your text, so two rows in the tag panel can become one.
- In the search panel, replacement text without a regular expression is now inserted exactly
  as typed: `$$`, `$&` and the rest are no longer special. With a regular expression, `$&`,
  `` $` ``, `$'` and `$<name>` are no longer special; use `$0` and `${name}`, and write `${1}a`
  rather than `$1a`, which now reads as a group named `1a`.
- A file window's close button now closes only that window, and a tab with unsaved changes, or
  an Untitled tab, can no longer be dragged out into its own window.
- A trusted plugin written for the old editor calls (`getContent`, `setContent`) stops working
  until its author updates it.

---

# New and improved

## Read your notes from a terminal

`baram`, the program that opens the editor, now also answers questions about a vault from a
terminal. It is meant for scripts and AI agents. Nine commands — `vaults`, `files`, `read`,
`search`, `tags`, `tag`, `tasks`, `backlinks` and `links` — print one item per line with its
fields separated by tabs, or one JSON object with `--json`; `read` prints the file itself.
They read the files on disk, so the app does not need to be open, and edits you have not saved
in it are not seen. None of the commands changes a file in your vault or the app's settings.

- On macOS, run `/Applications/Baram.app/Contents/MacOS/baram`. The Linux `.deb` package puts
  `baram` on your `PATH`. On Windows the commands are built in, but it has not been confirmed
  yet that their output reaches a terminal.
- `--vault` names the vault to read, by its path or by the name the app shows for it. Without
  it, the registered vault or folder that contains the current directory is read. A vault that
  cannot be found is an error; the commands never fall back to the vault that was last open in
  the app.
- With no arguments, or with an absolute path or a URL as its first argument, `baram` opens the
  app as before. **Any other first argument is now read as a command**: `baram notes.md`, which
  used to open a window, now stops with a usage error and opens none.

The new **Command line** page of the documentation lists every command, its output and its
error codes, and has an example to paste into an agent's instructions.

## Let an AI client read your notes

`baram mcp` serves the same nine commands as tools to an AI client that speaks the Model
Context Protocol (MCP), such as Claude Code. The client starts the server itself; you add it
to the client's settings once. The tools only read.

- **You choose what the client may read.** Without `--vault`, every vault and folder registered
  in the app is open to it. With `--vault`, only the vaults you name, and the first one is the
  default.
- **The tools reach less than the commands do**, because a model picks their arguments.
  `read_note` opens notes only — `.md` and `.markdown` files, not hidden ones and none inside
  `node_modules` — where the command line's `read` reads any text file in the vault.
- Long lists and long notes come back a page at a time.
- It has been tried with Claude Code. The setup the documentation gives for Claude Desktop has
  not been tried with Claude Desktop yet, and on Windows the server has not been verified yet.

The new **MCP server** page of the documentation shows how to add it to Claude Code and to
Claude Desktop.

## Plugins can do more

- **Right-click and slash menus.** A plugin can add its commands to the editor's right-click
  menu, where they come last, below a line, grouped by plugin and with the plugin's name beside
  each item, and to the slash menu, where they come last under “Plugin ·” and the plugin's name.
- **Shortcuts for plugin commands.** You can give a command a plugin declares a keyboard
  shortcut in Settings › Keybindings, under **Plugins**. A plugin cannot choose a key itself,
  and a key that one of Baram's own commands has on that page cannot be given to a plugin
  command. A few keys Baram uses that are not listed there, such as the zoom keys, are not
  checked.
- **Code blocks a plugin draws.** A plugin can draw the fenced code blocks of the languages it
  declares. Its install dialog lists them under **Code blocks it draws:**, and an update that
  adds a language asks you again. A drawn block is labelled with the plugin's name and has a
  **Show source** button. HTML and PDF exports use the drawing; a block that was never drawn
  exports as ordinary code.
- **Sidebar panels for sandboxed plugins.** A sandboxed plugin can have up to three sidebar
  panels, which Baram draws for it. The activity bar button names the panel, then “Plugin ·”
  and the plugin's name.
- **The file tree.** A plugin with the new permission “Show icons and badges on files in the
  file tree, and add items to its right-click menu” can mark a row with a badge, an icon, a
  colour or a tooltip, and add items to the menu a file or folder row opens.

When this version was released (8 November 2026), none of the plugins in the marketplace used
any of these yet.

## Light or dark, whatever your system uses

Settings › Appearance has a new **Mode** row below the theme gallery: **System**, **Light** or
**Dark**. It picks which palette a theme that has both a light and a dark one shows — Baram's
default palettes, or Baram Hangul from the theme registry, for example — so the editor can stay
dark while your system is light, or the other way round. **System** follows your system, as
before.

- The row is hidden while you use a theme that has only one mode, because that theme's mode
  always applies. Your choice is kept and applies again when you switch back to a theme that
  has both.
- It is your setting, not an appearance dial: a theme cannot suggest it, and **Export Look as
  Theme...** does not include it.
- The **System (Auto)** card in the gallery is now called **Baram Default**, because “System”
  is now a mode. It is the same theme, and it stays selected if you were using it.

## Table column resizing can be turned off

Settings › Markdown has a new switch under **Tables**: **Adjustable table column widths**, on
by default. With it off, the handles on column borders go away and a click near a border is an
ordinary click, so no new width comment (`<!-- colwidths:... -->`) is written above a table.

Turning it off also removes the widths you set from the tables in your open tabs. Those tables
go back to widths that fit their content, and their tabs are marked unsaved; once they are
saved, the files no longer hold the width comments. The switch itself writes nothing to disk:
the active tab is saved by autosave if you use it, and another tab when you save it. A file
you open while the switch is off keeps its widths, and its comment stays when you save.

## Backlinks keep up with changes made outside Baram

The link index behind the backlinks panel and the graph did not notice changes another program
made to your notes — git, a sync tool, another editor. Now, when files change in a vault Baram
is watching (the active one and any you opened this session), Baram updates its link index
within about two seconds, and the panel and the graph read it again.

The panel's **Unlinked mentions** are now searched again when another note's text changes,
even when its links did not, and no longer every time you save the note you are looking at —
that search reads every other note in the vault.

## Rename a PDF or an image

Renaming a PDF, an image or another file that is not text failed with “Rename failed: …”. It now
renames the file and, as for a note, rewrites the wikilinks and block references that point at
it. A PDF's highlights and its companion note move with it, and a tab open on a file that moved
follows it.

When you rename a file (not a folder), some links Baram does not rewrite are now reported
instead of left to break without a word. A markdown link or image (`[text](file)`,
`![alt](file)`) or an HTML `src` or `poster` attribute that points at the renamed file is left
as it is, and the note holding it is counted in “Renamed, but … file(s) may still link to the
old name.”

## Vim moves more like Vim

With **Vim Keybindings** on, in the WYSIWYG editor:

- `j` and `k` remember the column you started from when they pass a shorter line, an empty
  line, a formula or a table row, and go back to it on a longer line. After `$`, they follow
  the end of each line.
- `Esc` out of insert mode puts the cursor on the last character you typed, and collapses a
  selection you made in insert mode. The cursor no longer rests past the end of a line after
  `x`, `d$` or a click there.
- `gg`, `G` and `:N` land on the first non-blank character of the line, as `^` does.
- `dj`, `yj` and `cj` on the last line, and `dk`, `yk` and `ck` on the first, now do nothing,
  as in Vim. `dj` and `dk` used to delete the line.
- The normal-mode cursor now shows on an empty line in front matter and between two hard line
  breaks, where it was invisible.

## Faster in a few places

- **Find in a long document.** While Find has a search in it, every keystroke searches the
  document again. The step that turns the document into text for that search took time that
  grew with the document's length times its number of blocks; it now grows with its length
  only. Closing Find from the menu now also ends the
  search and clears its highlights — before, only the bar went away and the hidden search kept
  running on every edit.
- **AI chat.** Baram saved the whole chat history for every piece of a reply as it streamed
  in. It now saves at most once every 250 ms while a reply streams, and at once when the reply
  ends, fails or is stopped. Text appears as fast as before. Quitting and reloading wait up to
  3 seconds for the history to be saved. If Baram stops unexpectedly in the middle of a reply,
  the last quarter of a second or so of it may not have been saved.
- **Startup.** The formula fonts that HTML and PDF exports embed are no longer loaded when Baram
  starts, only the first time you export a document that has a formula.
- **`journal-photos` blocks** draw each photo from a smaller copy, chosen by the layout and the
  number of columns, instead of decoding the full photo. A photo shows as an empty square
  until its smaller copy is ready, and an animated GIF or WebP larger than that copy shows its
  first frame. Exporting the block to HTML or PDF now uses the same copies, in the same grid as
  on screen, except that a one-row strip wraps into rows in a PDF.
- **Closing a tab lets go of the file's text.** Baram kept the text of every file you had opened
  in memory until it quit, and read a closed file again whenever it changed on disk. In AI
  chat, `@folder:` still puts in the text of the files open in tabs and lists the rest by
  path, so a file you have closed is now listed by path, where before its text went in if you
  had opened it this session. Separately, `@file:` now reads a file that is not open in a tab
  from disk, so a file you never opened goes in with its text; before, it went in as its path,
  or with text Baram kept from earlier in the session.

## For plugin authors

This release adds a lot to the plugin API. Set `engines.baram` to `>=0.8.0` in a plugin that
uses any of it: v0.7.7 then refuses to install it. Without that floor, v0.7.7 still refuses a
manifest that declares the new `codeblocks` or `filetree` capability (“unknown capability”),
but installs one that uses the rest of the new API, which is not there for it to call.

- **One editor API for both tiers.** `context.editor` is now the same asynchronous API in
  trusted and sandboxed plugins: `getMarkdown`, `getText`, `getSelection`, which now also
  returns a `ref` for replacing exactly that range later, the new `insertMarkdown`, which
  inserts parsed markdown at the selection or at a `ref`, `insertText` and `setMarkdown`.
  Refusals come with a `code` to branch on (the page names the main errors that carry none). **A
  trusted plugin written for the old synchronous calls breaks**: `getContent()` and
  `setContent()` are gone (the old `setContent` emptied the document), and `insertText` inserts
  the characters as they are instead of reading them as HTML. The “Context: commands, editor,
  files, events” page has a table for moving over. When this version was released, neither
  plugin in the marketplace used the removed calls.
- **Menus and shortcuts.** `contributions.menu` (up to 5 items) and `contributions.slash` (up to
  10) put commands you declare in `contributions.commands` into the editor's right-click menu
  and the slash menu. A `menu` item with `when: "selection"` shows only over selected text.
  Users assign keys to your commands; a plugin cannot.
- **Code block renderers.** With the `codeblocks` capability and `contributions.codeBlocks` (up
  to 10 languages), `context.codeBlocks.register(lang, render)` draws fenced blocks of those
  languages from the `{ html, css? }` your renderer returns, which Baram sanitizes and draws in
  a shadow root. A language Baram draws itself (`mermaid`, `query`, `svg`, `journal-…`) or
  already highlights cannot be declared. See “Code block renderers”.
- **Sidebar panels for sandboxed plugins.** `contributions.panels` (up to 3, with `sidebar`)
  and `context.ui.setPanel(id, { html, css? })`, with the same sanitizing and click handling
  as code blocks. A trusted manifest that declares `panels` is refused; trusted plugins keep
  `ui.addSidebarPanel`. See “Sidebar panels”.
- **The file tree.** With `filetree`, `context.ui.setFileDecorations`, `clearFileDecorations`
  and `defineFileIcon` put badges, icons, colours and tooltips on rows, in both tiers, and
  `contributions.fileMenu` (up to 5) adds items to a row's right-click menu, whose command
  receives the item clicked or the items selected. See “File tree decorations”.
- **Index reads.** `context.index` — `backlinks`, `links`, `tags`, `notesWithTag`, `tasks` and
  `search` — reads a vault's links, tags, tasks and text as saved on disk. `files` or
  `files:readonly` opens it. See “Context: index”.
- **Events.** `vault:changed` says a vault's contents changed, including changes made outside
  Baram, so you can read again. `file:rename` and `file:delete` report renames, moves and
  deletions made in Baram. All three need `files` or `files:readonly`, not `events`.
- **Editable file viewers.** A trusted plugin's file viewer can now edit the file it shows:
  register it with `editable: true` and a `getText` function; the plugin needs `files`. Baram
  still does the saving, the unsaved mark and autosave. See “Editable file viewers”.
- **New examples** in the Baram repository: `link-count`, `backlinks-block`, `tree-badges` and
  `sketch-pad`.

---

# Fixed

## Unsaved work

- **Updating could discard unsaved changes.** **Install & Restart** went straight to
  installing, and installing ends Baram, so anything not yet saved was lost. Once the download
  finishes, Baram now asks about unsaved documents first — **Save & Install**, **Don't Save**
  or **Cancel** — and after **Cancel**, pressing the button again uses the update it already
  downloaded. This check is part of v0.8.0, so it protects the updates after this one. The
  update to v0.8.0 is run by v0.7.7, which does not ask.
- **Text in an Untitled tab did not count as unsaved**, so quitting, reloading, closing the
  workspace, `Cmd+W` / `Ctrl+W` and the tab's close button discarded it without asking. They
  ask now; an empty Untitled tab still closes quietly. Saving such a tab now saves what it
  holds: Save As on an Untitled tab in the background used to write an empty file.
- **Close Other Tabs and Close Tabs to the Right** closed tabs with unsaved changes without
  asking. They now ask, with **Save & Close Tabs**.
- **File windows** (a tab dragged out into a window of its own):
  - Their close button could quit the whole app. It now closes that window only, and asks
    first — **Save & Close**, **Don't Save** or **Cancel** — when the window has unsaved
    changes.
  - Quitting and installing an update did not count what file windows held. They do now, and
    **Save & Quit** or **Save & Install** saves in those windows too, waiting up to 10 seconds;
    if one cannot save, quitting or installing stops.
  - Menu commands chosen in a file window acted on the main window's active tab: `Cmd+W` /
    `Ctrl+W` closed a tab you were not looking at, and **Insert** › **Bold** changed its
    document out of sight. **Save**, **Close Tab**, **Toggle Source Mode** and the **Insert**
    menu now act on the file window. Commands that cannot work there, such as **Save As...**,
    **Export...**, **Find & Replace** and **Close Workspace**, say “This isn't available in a
    separate window.” Others, such as **New File** and **Settings...**, bring the main window
    to the front.
  - Closing the last main-window tab of a file you had opened on its own, while a file window
    also had it open, or closing the vault a file window's file belongs to, made the file
    window's saves fail until the file or its vault was opened again in the main window, or
    Baram restarted. They keep working now.
  - A file window marked its document unsaved as soon as it opened, and autosave never cleared
    the mark. It now starts clear, and autosave clears it. In source mode, `Cmd+S` / `Ctrl+S`
    saved the older document; it saves what you see now. Undo right after a file window opened
    no longer empties the document.
  - A tab with unsaved changes, or an Untitled tab, can no longer be dragged out into its own
    window. The new window reads the file from disk, so the unsaved text would have been lost.
    Baram says “Save this tab before moving it to its own window.”
- **Source mode.** Typing and then switching to source mode within the autosave delay could
  write the older document and mark the tab saved, and closing the tab then lost what you had
  typed in source mode. The **Insert** menu no longer changes the hidden document while you are
  in source mode — what it inserted was wiped when you switched back. It says “This works on
  the document. Leave source mode first.”
- **Typing while a save was being written** left the tab marked saved, so closing it then
  discarded what you had just typed. The tab stays unsaved now, and the next save writes it.
- **Renaming a file while an autosave was waiting** brought the file back under its old name.
  The save now goes to the new name.
- **One tab's text could end up in another file.** After a code or other non-markdown tab was
  reloaded, typing in a tab whose file had been deleted outside Baram could save the other
  file's text into it. A link that a rename rewrote in a tab waiting behind a non-markdown tab
  could be lost when you saved, and reloading a large document while it was still loading
  repeated some of its blocks.

## Files that could be overwritten

- **A journal entry Baram could not read was replaced by the template.** When today's entry,
  or one opened from the calendar or a date link, existed but could not be read — not valid
  UTF-8, or refused by the system — Baram treated it as missing and wrote a new entry over it.
  It now writes nothing unless the file is really not there. Weekly notes and the Work Log had
  the same fault and are fixed too.
- **New File in the file tree replaced a file that already had that name** with an empty one.
  On a disk that ignores case, as macOS and Windows disks usually do, `README.md` replaced
  `readme.md` the same way. It now changes nothing and tells you that the name already exists.
- **A wikilink that found no note could overwrite one.** `Cmd`+clicking such a link (`Ctrl`
  on Windows and Linux), or choosing `Create "…"` in the `[[` menu, wrote `# name` over a file
  already at that path. It now leaves the file alone and says that the file already exists,
  but this link does not find it, and that no new note was created. The `[[` menu also no
  longer offers `Create "…"`
  for a link a click would already open.

## Text that changed when saved

- **Brackets were saved with backslashes.** `[important]`, `[1]` or `[@smith2020, p. 3]` in
  ordinary text was saved as `\[important]` and so on. It is now saved as you typed it, except
  where a bracket could start something, such as a footnote (`[^`), a task box at the start of
  a line, or a link. Pandoc exports still show such brackets as text.
- **`$_GET and $_POST` in plain text was saved so that it reopened as a formula.** It is saved
  as text now.
- **Inside code and formulas, a backslash before `#` was dropped** (`\#define` became
  `#define`), and `&#x20;` at the end of a line in code, formulas and HTML blocks was removed.
  Both are kept now.
- **Highlight, subscript and superscript** (`==…==`, `~…~`, `^…^`) saved their text without
  escaping it, so `[a](b)` in a highlight reopened as a link and `<b>` disappeared. The text is
  escaped now, so a file that has such text can change the next time it is saved
  (`==a*b==` becomes `==a\*b==`) and reopens the same. Where the short form could not be read
  back, Baram saves a `<mark>`, `<sub>` or `<sup>` tag instead.
- **Strikethrough** with a space at either end, or with a punctuation mark at an end and a
  letter right outside it, was saved in a form that did not close (`a ~~e ~~f`), and reopened
  without the strikethrough. It now reopens as it was.
- **A backslash before a letter next to bold or italic text** turned that letter into a
  character code such as `&#x6E;`. Fixed.
- **An HTML block you edited stayed one HTML block** even when the file would read it back
  differently: a `<div>` with a blank line inside reopened as three blocks. When you leave the
  block, Baram now turns text that reads back as other blocks into those blocks — undo brings
  the HTML block back — and otherwise keeps your text and tells you it will read differently,
  or may merge with the blocks next to it, when the file is opened again.
- **A quote, callout or footnote whose first block was HTML** lost everything inside it when
  saved; a quote was left as a lone `>`. **A paragraph or heading that started with a footnote
  reference**, in a file that defines the footnote, lost the text after it. Both keep their
  text now. One case got worse: an `<img>` tag right after that footnote reference
  (`[^1] <img src="a.png">`) was kept as an image in v0.7.7, and is now not shown and is
  removed when the file is saved. An `<img>` or `<video>` tag in a paragraph that also has
  formatting or other inline content (bold, italic, strikethrough, code, a formula, a link, a
  footnote reference, or a character reference such as `&amp;`) was already not shown and
  removed on save, and still is. So is a `<br>`, or another HTML tag Baram does not read such
  as `<span>`, in a paragraph or heading with no `<img>` or `<video>` tag.
- **Clicking a table's column border without dragging** wrote a column-width comment into the
  file. Only a drag that changes a width does now.

## Links, backlinks and renames

- **References with a path** — `[[./note]]`, `[[../folder/note]]`, `((folder/note#^id))` — did
  not appear in the backlinks panel, and renaming the note or a block ID missed them. They
  appear and are rewritten now.
- **Renaming a note no longer rewrites links into another vault** (`[[work::note]]`), which it
  used to break, and they are no longer listed as backlinks of a local note of that name. If
  two registered vaults share a name, links that start with it are left alone, and renaming a
  note reports the files in its vault that hold them.
- **Changing only the case of the letters A to Z in a name** (`Note.md` to `note.md`) failed
  with “already exists”
  on macOS and Windows, and so, on macOS, did changing only how its letters are composed in
  Unicode. Both work now. **A new name containing `/`** used to move the file into
  another folder and quietly break its relative links; it is refused now.
- **The backlinks panel lists files by path and line**, instead of an order that could change
  after a save.
- **Names stored decomposed.** Some macOS tools store Korean and accented names in decomposed
  Unicode (NFD), so `[[회의록]]` typed in a note did not find `회의록.md`. A link now finds such
  a note when you click it, in previews and embeds, in the `[[` menu, the Quick Switcher, tree
  search and `@file:`, in backlinks, the graph and unlinked mentions, and when renaming. Names
  Baram writes into a link — from the `[[` menu, Tab completion, **Copy as Wikilink** in the
  file tree, **Copy wikilink** in the graph, **Copy link** in the block menu or **Link** in
  unlinked mentions — are written composed.
- **`Cmd`+clicking a wikilink** (`Ctrl`+click on Windows and Linux) could open the `[[`
  suggestion menu instead of the note, and so could a plain click on a date link. Both go to the
  note now.
- **A PDF's backlinks** now count the links that name it with its extension — `[[Paper.pdf]]`,
  `![[Paper.pdf]]`, with a path, a heading or display text — and no longer `[[Paper]]`, which
  names a note called Paper.
- **A note's own block reference** (`((#^id))`) could resolve to another note of the same name.
  It resolves to its own note now.
- **Renaming `old.md` to `old.txt`** left `[[old]]` pointing at nothing. It becomes
  `[[old.txt]]`.
- **Renaming in the file tree and pressing Enter** showed “Rename failed: …” although the item
  had been renamed, and pressing Esc after typing a new name renamed the item anyway. Enter
  now renames once, and Esc leaves the old name.
- **Suggestions after `[[./` or `[[../`** were always “No matching pages” on macOS and Linux,
  and on Windows `[[./` could offer the files of every folder in the vault. The `[[` menu now
  lists the files of the folder the prefix points to, counted from the open note's folder.
- **On Windows, clicking a relative wikilink** such as `[[./plan]]` or `[[../other/far]]` did
  not open the note: Baram treated it as a link that finds no note. In a file opened on its
  own outside a vault, `[[plan]]` pointed at `/plan.md` instead of the file next to it. Both
  now resolve against the open note's folder, and the `[[work::` menu groups another vault's
  notes by folder on Windows too.

## Tags and front matter

- **A front-matter tag written with `#`** (`tags: ["#solo"]`) is now the tag `solo` — in the
  tag panel, the graph, the tag bar and the command line — and counts together with `#solo` in
  your text. It used to be a separate tag `#solo`, shown as `##solo` in the tag bar. A colour
  you gave the `#solo` row in the tag panel moves to `solo`, unless `solo` already had one.
- **A comment after a list item** (`- plain # memo`) was read as part of the tag, making a tag
  called `plain # memo`. It is the tag `plain` now, as YAML reads it, and renaming the tag keeps
  the comment.
- **Items of a `tags:` list that was not indented** were not counted. They are now.
- **Renaming a tag** now changes every spelling of it in front matter, written the way you
  wrote it, and nothing else. It used to miss quoted items in a block list, and could change
  other fields, a list in the body or the start of a longer tag. A new name that a tag cannot
  have is refused, instead of being written into front matter YAML could not read.
- **The tag bar, the properties panel and new Zettel notes wrote front matter YAML could not
  read**: adding `x` to `tags: ["#solo"]` with the tag bar wrote `tags: [#solo, x]`, and a value
  or a Zettel title such as `Plan: v2` was written without quotes. They write front matter YAML
  reads back now. When the tag bar or the properties panel cannot change a field safely, it
  leaves it alone and says so — for the tag bar, “These tags can't be changed here. Edit them in
  the front matter YAML.”
- **Editing one value in the properties panel** wrote the whole front matter again, losing
  block lists, comments and nested values. Only that key's lines change now. An `aliases:`
  block list shows as items you can edit, where it showed as `""` and disappeared when edited.
- **A tag name with a space** (`my tag`) is no longer accepted where you type a tag name, since
  text in a note cannot spell it.

## Search

- **Replace in the search panel** (`Cmd+Shift+F` / `Ctrl+Shift+F`) found matches its own way,
  which could differ from the list: with **Match whole word**, **Replace All** could change a
  match the list did not show; a regular expression such as `^x` was applied to the whole file
  at once, not line by line as the list searches; and replacing the second match on a line
  changed the first. It now finds matches the way the list does, line by line and with the
  same whole-word rule, and a match's own button replaces that match. In a regular
  expression's replacement, use `$0` for the match and `${name}` for a named group. If a
  replace fails, the panel says why and searches again.
- **Match whole word with a regular expression** put the word boundaries around the expression
  without grouping it, so `a|b` found text starting with `a` or ending with `b`. It now finds
  the word `a` or the word `b`, in Find and in the search panel.
- **The preview of a very long match** in search results is now cut at 300 characters, with
  `…` where it is cut.

## Startup

- **Restoring at launch.** When Baram restored your vault at launch and the journal or the
  Zettel home note opened on startup, the vault tab moved to that space while the file tree
  stayed on your vault. **Restore last file** and **New file** under **On Launch** (Settings ›
  General) did the same as **Restore last folder** once Baram had a vault or folder to restore,
  and the file recorded as last opened was often not the one you were last looking at. Now the
  vault tab, the file tree and the active tab all show the restored vault, the journal entry or
  home note opens behind it, **Restore last file** reopens the file you were last looking at,
  and **New file** opens a new file in your last vault.
- **Opening a file from another vault** — from a wikilink, the task panel, recent files or your
  operating system — now switches the vault tab and the file tree to that vault too, not only
  the editor.

## Editor

- **The guide line under a numbered list item**, with **Align numbers** (the default) chosen
  for **List number alignment**, hung to the right of the number, near the period, and further
  right in deeper lists. It now hangs from the number. If you use the
  Bullet Threading plugin, update it to 2.1.1, which draws its highlight on the same line; when
  this version was released, the plugin registry offered 2.1.1.
- **Formulas in Mermaid labels** (`$$…$$`) showed as empty boxes. They now appear inside their
  node. MathML inside an SVG's `<foreignObject>`, in an `svg` code block or an HTML block, now
  appears too.
- **A table could be drawn at the column widths of another tab's table.** Switching tabs, or
  opening a file, could show a table that had no widths of its own at the widths of the table
  in the same place in the tab you left, and dragging one of its columns could then save those
  widths into the file. Each table now gets its own widths.

## Accessibility

- **VoiceOver read every file tree row as a group**, without its file name. It now reads the
  rows as items of a tree, with the file name and any plugin badge.

## Plugins

- **Pressing Esc to close a plugin's quick pick** could put an escape control character into
  the note in place of the selection, when the selection spanned paragraphs or was a whole
  block. Fixed.
- **On macOS, a sandboxed plugin could stop running** a few seconds after Baram last sent it a
  message, so its own timers stopped firing. On macOS 14 and later it keeps running now, though
  its repeating timers fire at most about once a second, because its window is hidden.

---

**Updating.** If you are on v0.7.7, **save your open documents — in file windows too — before
you press Install & Restart**: v0.7.7 runs this update itself, and it installs and restarts
without asking about unsaved changes. From v0.8.0 on, Baram asks first. Press **Install &
Restart** in the update dialog and Baram installs in place and restarts. If an install fails,
Baram opens the releases page instead.
